front: What are the four Red-Black Tree rules?
back: 1) Every node is red or black. 2) The root is black. 3) A red node never has a red child. 4) Every root-to-leaf path has the same number of black nodes.

front: What height guarantee does a Red-Black Tree provide?
back: Height ≤ 2·log(n+1), keeping search/insert/delete at Θ(log n) worst case.

front: Why use a shared sentinel node instead of null pointers in an RBT implementation?
back: It ensures every node always has valid left/right/parent references, removing most null-checking special cases from the algorithms.

front: What color is a newly inserted node in an RBT, before fixup?
back: Red — this can only violate rule 3 (red-red), never rule 4 (black-height), which fixup then repairs.

front: What real-world system uses a Red-Black Tree, and for what?
back: The Linux kernel's Completely Fair Scheduler (CFS) — keeps runnable processes ordered by virtual runtime.
